data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Granos' meaning 'grain', symbolizing strength and nourishment. In Christian tradition, it may be associated with the grain of wheat that falls to the ground and dies, only to rise again in new life. The name Grane carries the meaning “Strong, Gracious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Grane usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, gracious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: While the name "Grane" does not have any direct connection to Christian tradition, the Greek origin of the name "Granos" symbolizes the idea of 'grain' in Christianity. This biblical reference is often used metaphorically to describe the enduring quality of faith, and the transformative power of hardship. For instance, in John 12:24, Jesus speaks about a grain of wheat that must be planted in the ground and die before it can produce new life and yield a rich harvest. Consequently, the name "Grane", although uncommon, has a cultural significance in Christianity by reminding us of the symbolism of growth through adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name "Grane" can be interpreted as a reminder of the transformative power of faith and sacrifice. The grain of wheat dying and rising again represents the Christian belief in resurrection and eternal life. This symbolism encourages those bearing the name "Grane" to have faith in their struggles and trust that, like the grain of wheat, they too can rise above their hardships and emerge stronger and renewed. Additionally, it serves as a call to sow seeds of love, kindness, and generosity in our lives, knowing that the results will come to fruition in good time.
